bulletins.text: Temperatures climbed {delta} since yesterday. {players} have already migrated toward the sunniest corner of the hub.
It is {temp} outside - noticeably warmer than yesterday. Jackets are disappearing quickly.
A warmer afternoon has arrived at {temp}. {player} is already campaigning for more time outside.
Temperatures dropped {delta} since yesterday. {player} has suggested a campfire before anyone else can claim the warmest seat.
A cooler turn has taken hold at {temp}. The blankets have quietly started changing hands.
The temperature is down {delta} from yesterday. {players} are debating whether the patio is still worth it.
The weather is holding steady at {temp}. Even the forecast seems comfortable where it is.
Very little has changed outside today - {temp}, and almost exactly where yesterday left things.
At {temp}, the patio is winning. {players} have already claimed the best patch of sun.
The sun is still doing most of the work today. {player} appears to have unofficially reserved a sunbathing spot.
The sun has been shining for {streak} days. The hub is starting to treat clear skies as a house rule.
Another clear day makes it {streak} in a row. {players} have stopped checking whether they need jackets.
Sun and cloud have been taking turns all afternoon. {player} keeps moving seats to stay in the light.
Cloud has held over the hub all day. It is still {temp}, but nobody seems in a hurry to leave the sofa.
Another grey day makes {streak} in a row. {player} has formally requested a little sunlight.
The mist has been slow to lift today. The world beyond the garden still looks slightly unfinished.
The fog is still clinging to the hub. {players} can barely make out the far side of the garden.
The drizzle never quite became proper rain, but it has been enough to keep everyone hovering near the doors.
Showers keep passing through without committing to the day. {player} has given up trying to time a dry trip outside.
The hub has managed sunshine and rain at the same time. Half the garden is bright; the other half is getting wet.
A sun shower caught {players} outside. Neither seems entirely convinced they should run for cover.
Rain has everyone clustered indoors at {temp}. {player} has put something warm on and accepted the situation.
The rain is still tapping at the windows. Indoor plans have quietly won the afternoon.
Rain again - {streak} wet days in a row. The hub has become very good at inventing indoor plans.
The rain has intensified enough to erase any serious outdoor plans. {players} are watching it hammer the windows instead.
Thunder is getting closer. Nobody needed much convincing to bring the afternoon indoors.
The storm is still pressing against the hub. {player} is pretending the latest thunderclap did not make them jump.
Flurries have been coming and going all afternoon. {players} are waiting for one good burst before heading outside.
Snow is settling outside at {temp}. {players} are already debating who gets to leave the first footprints.
The garden is turning white. {player} has been checking the window often enough for everyone to notice.
The cloud has started to break apart. Brighter patches are finally reaching the garden.
The worst of the weather has moved on. {players} are cautiously rediscovering the outdoors.
Sunlight has caught the last of the rain and a rainbow has appeared over the hub. {players} made it to the window almost immediately.
The shower is moving away, but it left a rainbow behind. For once, everyone is looking in the same direction.
A brief rainbow has formed beyond the garden after the rain. {player} was the first to spot it.
It is only {temp} outside. The warmest seats in the hub have become unexpectedly strategic territory.
The temperature has reached {temp}. Shade and cold drinks are suddenly the most valuable resources in the hub.
It is a mild {temp} outside. {players} have suggested taking the next quiet conversation outdoors.
